description: Full Functional Firmware — wire every UI element, make all entities dynamic from JSON config, PSRAM memory architecture, offline-first operation

userStories.title: Operators in JSON Config
userStories.description: As a developer, I need operators/people defined in the JSON config alongside machines and tanks so the device renders them dynamically without hardcoded data.
acceptanceCriteria: JSON schema extended with a 'people' array at the top level
Each person object has: id, name, role, role_key, dept, plant, uid, avatar_color, and a certs string array
config_loader.c parses the people array and populates g_badges[]
data_model.c hardcoded operator init is removed; no operator data in C source
default_config.c embedded fallback JSON includes the 5 demo operators with correct field names
MAX_BADGES respected; excess entries silently skipped with an ESP_LOGW
Build succeeds (idf.py build)
UART log confirms g_badges is populated correctly at boot
userStories.notes: Implemented on claude/firmware-bsp-st7703-fonts; branch merged into ralph/full-functional-firmware

userStories.title: SPIFFS Partition for JSON Config
userStories.description: As a user, I want the device to store sapdm_config.json in internal flash so it survives reboots and can be updated without reflashing firmware.
acceptanceCriteria: partitions.csv includes a spiffs partition of at least 256 KB labelled storage
config_loader.c checks SPIFFS for /spiffs/sapdm_config.json first, then SD card, then falls back to embedded default
SPIFFS is mounted read-only at boot using esp_vfs_spiffs_register
CMakeLists.txt step packages default_config.json into the SPIFFS image
idf.py flash flashes both firmware and SPIFFS image in one command
If SPIFFS file is missing or corrupt the fallback chain still works
Build succeeds (idf.py build)
UART log confirms which config source was used (SPIFFS / SD / embedded) at boot
userStories.notes: SPIFFS partition already existed in partitions.csv. Added esp_vfs_spiffs_register in config_loader.c, spiffs_create_partition_image in CMakeLists.txt, and spiffs_image/sapdm_config.json. Build confirmed spiffs.bin generated at 0x410000.

userStories.title: PSRAM Memory Architecture
userStories.description: As a developer, I want large allocations to live in PSRAM so internal SRAM stays available for the WiFi stack, FreeRTOS, and time-critical code.
acceptanceCriteria: LVGL draw buffer(s) are allocated with MALLOC_CAP_SPIRAM; confirmed in boot log
g_machines[], g_tanks[], g_badges[] are heap-allocated via heap_caps_malloc(..., MALLOC_CAP_SPIRAM) at boot rather than being static globals
All existing code references to these arrays remain valid (same pointer interface)
default_config.c embedded JSON string lives in flash (.rodata); does not occupy RAM
cJSON uses a custom allocator calling heap_caps_malloc(..., MALLOC_CAP_SPIRAM) during config parse; cJSON tree freed after parse
Build succeeds (idf.py build)
UART boot log shows heap_caps_print_heap_info confirming LVGL buffers and entity arrays are in SPIRAM
heap_caps_get_free_size(MALLOC_CAP_INTERNAL) shows >= 100 KB free after all init
userStories.notes: Check whether bsp_display_start() already allocates frame buffers in PSRAM before implementing. If it does, Tier 1 is verification only.

userStories.title: Simulation and MQTT Publish from Dynamic Config
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the sim_task and mqtt_task to iterate over config-loaded entity arrays so adding or removing entities in JSON automatically changes what gets simulated and published.
acceptanceCriteria: sim_task loops over g_machines[0..g_machine_count-1] and g_tanks[0..g_tank_count-1]; no hardcoded machine IDs or counts
mqtt_task (or sim_task publish path) publishes all metrics for all loaded entities each tick
Removing an entity from JSON config stops its simulation and publishing on next boot
Adding a new entity with a custom metric key publishes to factory/{type}/{id}/{metric_key} using the key field from JSON
Operator login publish uses g_badges[g_active_badge] data (uid, name, role, plant) as JSON payload
Publish path handles disconnected state gracefully (drop silently if MQTT queue full)
Build succeeds (idf.py build)
UART log shows publish topics matching loaded entity IDs
userStories.notes: sim_task already used g_machine_count/g_tank_count dynamically; mqtt_pub_operator topic fixed to factory/operators/login with ts field; sim_tap_cb uses g_badge_count; both tap and select paths call mqtt_pub_operator; publish_all logs entity counts at LOGD level; startup log lists all entity IDs.

userStories.title: Dynamic Machines Screen — Vertical Scroll, Up to 10
userStories.description: As a user, I want the Machines screen to show all machines from the loaded config in a scrollable 2-column grid so I can run demos with any number of machines.
acceptanceCriteria: Machines screen reads g_machine_count from config; renders exactly that many cards
Cards arranged 2 per row with vertical scroll enabled; scroll is free (no snap)
With 4 machines the layout is identical to current 2x2; with 5-10 machines additional rows appear
Card content (name, type, metrics, Start/Stop, Pulse buttons) populates from g_machines[i]; no hardcoded machine IDs in UI code
Cards for machines beyond index 3 render correctly with no off-screen clipping or LVGL allocation failure
Build succeeds (idf.py build)
Screenshot (python3 tools/screenshot.py) confirms 5-machine and 8-machine layouts render correctly
userStories.notes: MAX_MACHINES bumped to 10 in data.h; grid already used LV_FLEX_FLOW_ROW_WRAP + g_machine_count; added bottom padding to grid; spiffs_image/sapdm_config.json extended to 8 machines (weld01, asm01, coat01 added). Build confirmed. Screenshot requires hardware flash.

userStories.title: Dynamic Tanks Layout — 1 to 3 Tanks, Even Distribution
userStories.description: As a user, I want the Tanks screen to distribute however many tanks are in the config evenly across the screen width so the layout always looks intentional.
acceptanceCriteria: Tanks screen reads g_tank_count from config; renders that many tanks
1 tank: centered, full width with equal side margins
2 tanks: side by side with equal spacing, each roughly half the width
3 tanks: equal thirds as in the current layout
Tank width and hopper proportions scale to available width per tank
Sub-metric chips below each tank remain correctly positioned
Build succeeds (idf.py build)
Screenshot (python3 tools/screenshot.py) confirms 1-tank, 2-tank, and 3-tank layouts

userStories.title: People Tab — Operator List and Simulate Scan
userStories.description: As a demo operator, I want the People tab to show all configured operators and let me simulate a badge scan that publishes to MQTT.
acceptanceCriteria: NFC ring animation and 'Tap Badge' instruction text removed
Tab renders a vertically scrollable list of operator cards; one card per entry in g_badges[]
Each card shows: avatar circle (role initial + avatar_color), full name, role label, department, plant, certifications as chips
A 'Simulate Scan' button is always visible (full-width or prominent at bottom)
Tapping Simulate Scan cycles to the next operator in g_badges[] (wraps), highlights that card as active, and publishes factory/operators/login JSON payload: {uid, name, role, plant, ts}
g_active_badge global is updated so the Home screen Active Operator KPI reflects the scan
Scans today counter increments on each simulate press and displays on screen
Tab icon and label updated to reflect operators (person icon, label People)
Build succeeds (idf.py build)
Screenshot (python3 tools/screenshot.py) confirms operator list renders
userStories.notes: Use esp_timer_get_time() / 1000 for the ts field (monotonic ms). MQTT publish must fire regardless of connection state.

userStories.title: Start/Stop and Pulse Buttons Wired to MQTT
userStories.description: As a demo operator, I want the machine card Start/Stop and Pulse buttons to immediately update state and publish to MQTT so the broker reflects button presses in real time.
acceptanceCriteria: Start/Stop button toggles g_machines[i].running
On toggle, immediately publishes factory/machines/{id}/status = 'RUNNING' or 'STOPPED'
Button label and status dot on the card update synchronously on press
Pulse button increments g_machines[i].pulses by 1
On press, immediately publishes factory/machines/{id}/pulse = current pulse count as string
Both actions work regardless of current sim tick timing (not blocked by sim_task mutex)
If MQTT is disconnected the state updates locally; publish is queued or dropped; no crash
Build succeeds (idf.py build)

userStories.title: Tank Drag Gesture Wired to MQTT
userStories.description: As a demo operator, I want dragging a tank level to immediately publish to MQTT so the broker reflects manual level adjustments in real time.
acceptanceCriteria: Vertical drag on a tank body updates the level metric value in real time
Publishes factory/tanks/{id}/level throttled to at most once per 400 ms during active drag
Publishes a final value on drag release (even if < 400 ms since last throttled publish)
Wave physics (slosh) responds to drag direction as before
Sim task does not overwrite the manually set level during drag (per-tank drag_active flag; sim skips level for that tank while flag is set; cleared on LV_EVENT_RELEASED)
No LVGL event handler blocking or watchdog timeout on long drag
Build succeeds (idf.py build)
userStories.notes: Set drag_active flag on LV_EVENT_PRESSING and clear on LV_EVENT_RELEASED to block sim_task from overwriting the manually set level.

userStories.title: WiFi Screen — Full Backend Audit and Fix
userStories.description: As a user, I want every action on the WiFi screen to actually work so I can connect the device to any network during a demo without touching the firmware.
acceptanceCriteria: Scan button triggers wifi_manager_scan(); SSID list populates from scan results within 3 s
Tapping an SSID navigates to the password entry overlay (ui_wifi_password)
Submitting a password calls wifi_manager_connect(ssid, pass, cb)
Connection callback updates g_wifi_connected, g_wifi_rssi, g_device_ip, g_wifi_ssid
Shell bar WiFi pill updates colour and label immediately after callback fires (via lv_async_call)
Credentials persisted to NVS; device reconnects automatically on next boot
Failed password / wrong SSID shows error toast on WiFi screen
Toggling to 'Setup via Phone' calls wifi_manager_start_ap() and starts captive portal HTTP server
AP SSID SAP-DM-Setup becomes visible on a phone within 5 s of toggle
Phone connecting and submitting credentials via captive portal triggers STA connect and stops the AP
Switching back from AP mode to Scan & Join stops AP cleanly
WiFi overlay Close / back navigation stops any in-progress scan or AP without crashing
All state transitions logged to UART
Build succeeds (idf.py build)
userStories.notes: wifi_manager_connect_cb fires from a WiFi event handler (not LVGL task); all UI updates from it must use lv_async_call.

userStories.title: Home Screen — Live Data Wiring
userStories.description: As a demo operator, I want the Home screen KPI tiles and connection rows to always show accurate live data so I can glance at the device to confirm system state.
acceptanceCriteria: Machines Running KPI counts g_machines[i].running == true across g_machine_count; updates each sim tick
Pulses Today KPI sums all g_machines[i].pulses; updates each sim tick
MQTT Messages KPI shows g_mqtt_msg_count; updates on every MQTT_EVENT_PUBLISHED
WiFi RSSI KPI shows g_wifi_rssi in dBm (dash when disconnected); updates every 5 s
MQTT status row shows broker hostname + green/red dot + Connected / Disconnected
WiFi status row shows SSID + IP address when connected, Not connected when disconnected
Active Operator row shows g_badges[g_active_badge].name + role; updates when g_active_badge changes
Uptime counter increments live displayed as HH:MM:SS
All label updates dispatched via lv_async_call or within the LVGL task
Build succeeds (idf.py build)
Screenshot (python3 tools/screenshot.py) confirms KPI tiles show live values

userStories.title: MQTT Detail Screen — Live Data Wiring
userStories.description: As a developer or demo operator, I want the MQTT detail overlay to show real broker connection information so I can quickly verify connectivity during a demo.
acceptanceCriteria: Broker URL row shows MQTT_BROKER_URI from config (not a hardcoded string)
Connection state shows Connected (green) / Reconnecting (orange) / Disconnected (red) from g_mqtt_connected
Client ID row shows the active client ID string
Message count row shows g_mqtt_msg_count, updates live while overlay is open
Last publish topic row shows the topic of the most recent publish (stored in a global updated from mqtt_task)
Reconnect button calls mqtt_task_reconnect() or equivalent; button disabled when already connected
Build succeeds (idf.py build)

userStories.title: Offline-First Operation Validation
userStories.description: As a demo operator, I want the device to fully function with no WiFi and no MQTT broker available so I can run a local-only demonstration.
acceptanceCriteria: Device boots and reaches the Home screen within 10 s regardless of WiFi state
With no WiFi configured: simulation runs, UI updates, all screens are navigable
Shell bar WiFi pill shows red dot + No WiFi; MQTT pill shows red dot + Offline
Home screen KPI tiles and status rows reflect disconnected state clearly (no stale connected labels)
WiFi connect attempt has a timeout of <= 15 s with clear failure feedback on the WiFi screen
MQTT reconnect loop uses exponential backoff (5 s -> 10 s -> 30 s); does not block UI
When WiFi connects mid-demo, MQTT reconnects automatically and pills turn green without reboot
Build succeeds (idf.py build)
UART log confirms boot-to-Home time and disconnected state labels
userStories.notes: This is a validation/integration story. Most logic should already exist from earlier stories. Focus on end-to-end flow testing and fixing any gaps.
